clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his 60s presented with a 2-year history of gradually worsening spastic paraparesis, gait imbalance, frequent falls, back/leg spasms, and decreased functional endurance, without sensory symptoms. Neurological examination revealed hyperreflexia in all four extremities, positive Babinski reflexes bilaterally, and a positive left-sided Hoffman reflex, consistent with myelopathy. His gait imbalance rapidly progressed from needing a cane to a walker within 3 months. After 1.5 years, repeat spinal imaging (CT myelogram and non-contrasted MRI of the thoracic spine) identified an arachnoid web at vertebral levels T7-T8, characterized by a minimal dorsal indentation along the spinal cord, without an associated syrinx. Surgical intervention involved a T6-T8 laminectomy, revealing thickened arachnoid webbing at T7-T8 causing increased localized pressure and compression on the spinal cord. Five months post-surgery, his neurologist diagnosed him with cervical myelopathy from previous spinal cord compression by the arachnoid web.
